notes: All 50 complete blinded source reports personally read in five ten-report groups. All 600 target decisions were explicitly reasoned with individual exact source quotations and ambiguity notes before any batch034 draft/review access. No official gold or legacy annotations inspected. Scripts only assemble explicit decisions and verify source quotations, schema, hashes and exact UID coverage; no regex, NLI, automatic inference, default filling or cross-report propagation. All unfinished work remained outside initiative. Source defects, contradictory assertions, anatomy, severity, missing extent and acuity remain preserved. These report-derived weak labels require an independent source-first reviewer and are not image diagnostic rereads.

flags.issue: Compartment localization, cartilage depth/extent or unnamed grading remain incomplete. Do not infer target positives from bare OA, gradeII/III/IV, or cyst dimensions.

Literal intact-number debris corrupts some dimensions. At005 the high-grade cartilage lesion has separate readable 3x1.1cm dimensions; the cyst debris is not parsed. At022 high-grade wording conflicts with less-than-50% thickness and corrupted area; PF remains uncertain.

PF denudation and confluent medial/PF full-thickness cartilage loss use qualitative regional extent as an explicit weak-supervision inference. Independently verify against source; not a measured area.

Findings diagnose a lateral complex tear while impression says no meniscal tear; masked. Lateral partial-thickness fissuring is described as mild tricompartmental chondrosis in impression and treated below threshold; severity interpretation flagged.
Nearly complete radial posterior-root tear lacks explicit medial/lateral meniscus identity. Adjacent medial OA cannot assign laterality; both meniscal targets masked. Literal aa preserved.

Meniscal abnormal morphology versus isolated degeneration: definite prior tear with marked thinning, degeneration without evident rupture, mild extrusion, and gradeIII with volume loss/4mm extrusion require independent source consistency review. Every case reason recorded individually; no automatic extrusion rule.

Avulsion/impaction/insufficiency fracture morphology does not alone resolve acute timing; equivocal R/O fracture remains masked. Separate definite bone-contusion statements preserved. Review each source rather than transfer one fracture subtype rule.
Source conflicts: ACL grade2 in findings versus grade1 conclusion; no joint fluid followed by increased joint/suprapatellar fluid. Conflicting targets masked.
Explicit slight fraying or superficial cartilage findings are below threshold despite unkeyed grade or diagnostic hedge; preserve distinction from bare numbered grade.

Secondary synovial chondromatosis mentions synovial pathology but does not establish inflamed thickened lining; synovitis uncertain. Considerable joint fluid interpreted as moderate/large weak positive.
Mild patellofemoral joint fluid followed by ungraded suprapatellar/knee fluid was interpreted below threshold without inventing a higher grade; scope to be independently checked.
Baker cyst is directly diagnosed and called small despite atypical semitendinosus localization wording; anatomy is preserved, not repaired.
Bone negatives use explicit broader bone morphology/structure or absence of all osseous lesions. Normal marrow signal alone elsewhere supports contusion only and does not fill fracture.
